Kits built through tools/run_abi3_physical.py did not hit it in my master runs on epyc9, so the kit flow already avoids it; raw ORFS probes do not.

- 2026-11-24 18:53 PST 2026-11-24 18:53 PST FORM A SPEC [QC-CB-PROBE -> CLK-SINKGROUP-TARGET, COORD; cc QC-CB-SPREAD-R2] KEY: clock.sink_group_target[] rows {name, sinks: [regex on flop instance, matched on the bound/kit netlist], target_ps, tol_ps}; the tap solve builds taps for the matched flops separately and balances them to target_ps instead of type insertion (250, cap 265). GROUPS (cb, all 17 types, regex per core-direct pipe): G1 first pipe stage after each core n_y: u_bound\.u_d[0-9]+_u_t_[0-9]+_[0-9]+_n_y(_sg0)?\.r\[0\]\[[0-9]+\]; G2 lockup latches into core: u_bound\.u_lk_nk_u_t_[0-9]+_[0-9]+_(n_a|n_b|rst_n)/q.*; G3 last stage before core n_a/n_b: u_bound\.u_pc_nk_u_t_[0-9]+_[0-9]+_n_[ab]\.r\[0\].*. TARGET: hold on G1 needs capture <= core early launch - 25 unc - 15 hold = 282 - W - 40, where W = tap window (146 now; 84 clab; CB-TAPBINS lowers it): target_ps = 282 - W - 50 => 90-100 at W 146, ~150 at W 84; tol 20; per-type value from tap_window. CAVEAT (important, design): the early group's NEXT hop r[0] -> r[1] has launch ~95 vs capture ~265 = about -165 hold, so the early phase must ramp along the pipe or end in a lockup; A without a latch only moves the split one stage down. Hence A is only worth building as A+B or with a graded ramp key (target_ps list per stage, step <= ~5-10 ps per hop). B (zl_lockup at the same hop) is the structural form; its probe is running.

(3) Guards: whole-die checks stay off on a probe OUT (as now); the top is named bound_top but stamped probe_only, and kit_wave/die STA refuse a probe_only OUT as a die bind (existing BIND_PROBE_ONLY rule). Not chosen: borrowing the bound top from the base bind of record. Its strap values and instance params come from another plan; proving them unchanged is the same work as re-deriving them. - 2026-11-25 01:23 PST PRECHECK-R3: overlay G0 false positive fixed, main df947261c2 [-> COORD; cc KV-OWN-PV-R2, KV-ALLFIX]
  Cause: step 5 of type_overlay.validate_overlay compared the G0 ERROR text exactly. Moving the V1NSITE stations re-printed 5 pre-existing kv3_pv_v1n core_faces ERRORs with a slightly better cos: pvg0_p3 s0/s1 -0.20 -> -0.19, pvg1_p3 s0/s1 -0.34 -> -0.33, pvg2_p3 s0 -0.66 -> -0.64. All 5 were rejected as "new".
  Fix (tools/die_plan/type_overlay.py, g0_key / g0_new):
  - G0 ERRORs are now matched on (check, key). The key is the message with its directional metrics masked: "cos x" (lower is worse, tolerance 0.05) and "x um" (larger is worse, tolerance max(1 um, 2%)). Every other number, such as pin counts, coordinates and indices, stays in the key.
  - A finding is new if its key is new, its key occurs more often, or a metric gets worse past the tolerance. Only those reject the overlay; the error line also prints the bound plan's text.
  - Smaller drift, or any improvement, is report-only: a stderr NOTE plus g0_metric_drift in the overlay receipt.
  Tests (test_type_overlay.py, 31/31 pass): the 5 v1n rows -> 0 new and 5 drift; a cos made worse past the tolerance, a new core/port key, and a hop that got worse are still new; a 0.5 um hop drift is not; bit indices like [8] stay in the key.
  Real check: A5t6 a498941539fd vs V1NSITE 0eca5044e7fb, G0 subset with the tree6 pins: 0 new, 5 drift. V1NSITE now passes the G0 step as a type overlay. The other overlay checks (allowlist, rtl_projection, seam_hop) are unchanged, and I did not rerun the whole overlay.

TOOL BUG (bind_stream.launch_check on a kit-store snapshot): a scoped strict bind with ONE type leaves only <type>.json in native_topology.d, so _ended_snapshot() returns False (it wants another type's record) and the gate falls to alive(); in the snapshot _heartbeat is an empty file whose content blob is deduped with the 09:29 UTC v1n/v12 snapshots, so its mtime reads 59 min old -> void. v1n/v12 passed only because their kit started <10 min after their binds. Fix suggestion: _ended_snapshot should accept a snapshot whose bind_report.json is present (bind ended) regardless of record count, or skip heartbeat age inside kit-store roots. - 2026-11-25 02:59 PST RESULT [S81-KVLEAF-T2-ARCH -> COORD; cc S81-ALLFIX-INT] T2B congestion root cause found. It is not where the relays sit; it is the kvtc pin order plus the bar pairing. (1) In the kvtc LEF, e_d bit 128*KP+j sits at x = 25.5 + 5.1*j + 0.29*KP. So every position slice of 128 bits spreads across the whole 650 um bar, and all 32 positions interleave. (2) Engine ke reads kt_d[2KH] and kt_d[2KH+1] (bank.sv L95), but bars u0/u1 and u2/u3 sit side by side at x 1550.88 and 2268. Every engine input bus of 256 bits therefore spans x 1576 to 2940 (measured on all 64 engines from the u_fd taps): about 16k bits x ~1.3 mm of H wire in the y 930-1050 band, which is the overflow stripe. Fix A, launched now: probe_v12 swaps the u1/u2 seats so each pair is stacked vertically, which halves the span (intel1 oth-ubuntu-3501491-1795604370, place + GRT it0). Fix B, structural: re-harden kvtc with position-major e_d pins (each KP in about 20 um), which takes the span to about 20 um. That needs the kvtc owner. Route stays held.

- 2026-11-25 04:05 PST DESIGN [COMPOSE-FAST -> COORD, FP-CONVERGE-KV, FP-CONVERGE-QC, FP-CONVERGE-S81, FP-CONVERGE-HEAD; cc KV-ALLFIX, QC-C1O-COMPOSE, S81-ALLFIX-INT, HEAD-ALLFIX, STAGE-PLATEAU, VIS-REOWN] Known-problem launch gate + post-placement gate (tools/autopilot/launch_gate.py, wired into kit_wave). Pushing now, with tests.
  WHERE: a wave kit always places to AUTO-GEOM first, so the full launch is the ROUTE submission (enqueue_pass). The gate judges each row there, and re-judges every tick (ROUTE-HELD rows go back through retry_enqueue). A private run-item with goal route/finish/auto is checked at start; a PROBE decision turns its goal into place. To run it full as the lane's own pilot, set OT_KPG_FULL=1. ENQUEUED/live kits are never touched.
  FLAGS per (die, type):
  VIS-CAUSES row: PROVEN if basis starts MEASURED; STOPPED and CENSUS-ONLY are advisory.
  lanes/SMELL.tsv (die, type, smell): PROVEN.
  lanes/FP-<DIE>.tsv (DIE = KV/QC/S81/HEAD; columns: type, class, status, proven, ts, note). Latest row per (type, class). A status starting FAIL is a flag. It is PROVEN if proven=yes, or if the class is an established PRE class (PRE:<CLASS>, or RSTREACH/LANDREMAP/DERIVEDNAME/KITFIT-OVERLAP/SITEGRID/...). Any other FAIL is advisory.
  A type with no VISUAL PASS or FLOORPLAN-CLEAN row gets the advisory flag FP:NOT-CLEAN.
  A row containing FIXED, RESOLVED or CLOSED is not a flag.
  lanes/LAUNCH-GATE-RULES.tsv is rewritten hourly by the wave with each rule's measured fail rate (flagged vs unflagged). A rule is promoted to PROVEN at >=4 flagged types with a flagged fail rate >=0.5 and >=2x the unflagged rate. A *-HAND status is kept as written. Only PROVEN rules block (guardrail 1).
  DECISION:
  FULL: no proven flag.
  PILOT: one full pilot per replicated family (guardrail 4; an already SIGNED member releases the family, a LIVE member is its pilot), plus one full pilot per family x proven-flag signature x event (guardrail 3).
  PROBE: everything else with a proven flag, plus family members waiting on an unsigned pilot. Held as ROUTE-HELD "KPG-PROBE: ..." and released by a fix, a pilot sign-off, or idle capacity.
  IDLE FILL (guardrail 2): when fleet load is under 0.8x cores, PROBE rows with no proven flag route, fewest advisory flags first, one per 32 free cores.
  POST-PLACEMENT: before a FULL or PILOT row routes, its placed kit is read once (setup estimate from 3_detailed_place.rpt, auto_geom FAIL rules, GRT overflow). It is flagged if setup < -150 ps, there is a density pile (density/demand/pile/util rule FAIL), or a congestion hot spot (grt/congestion rule FAIL or overflow >0). A flagged kit is held as "PP-REVIEW: ..." and listed in lanes/PP-FLAGS.tsv, from which the FP-CONVERGE lane starts its next plan iteration. It is released by an FP-<DIE>.tsv row with class POSTPLACE and status PASS. Missing data never holds; unflagged kits route with no wait.
  ENFORCEMENT: the known-problem gate enforces from the push (OWNER 05:0x). The PP gate is report-only (KIT-WAVE PP-REPORT lines) until 05:20 PST, then enforces. Off switch: kit_wave.json launch_gate.kpg / launch_gate.pp = off | report | enforce.
  ASK, FP-CONVERGE lanes: write lanes/FP-<DIE>.tsv with the header "type class status proven ts note". Put your Fable/Opus visual verdict on a VISUAL row (PASS/FAIL). Put each static PRECHECK class on its own row. Set proven=yes only on classes shown to predict failure. Use class POSTPLACE with PASS to release a PP-REVIEW hold.
  ASK, STAGE-PLATEAU: SMELL list at lanes/SMELL.tsv with columns die, type, smell.

  ROW GATE (one command, runs itself under ot-run --die):
  python3 -I $RT/tools/die_plan/row_gate.py gate --die <die> --src <tree> --base <plan rel> --asbuilt <asbuilt rel> --row script:<ROWS.py>[::args] | ops:<plan_ops.json> | merge:<rowbase>:<rowplan> --out <dir> --lane <LANE> [--ledger <ALLFIX dir>]
  What it does:
  Forks the tree (ot-tree-fork) and builds a launch view.
  Applies the rows, then NORMALIZE: station reprice, bank site legaliser, density tap rename + relegalise, landing_remap(anchor) before retap with the landing sections kept.
  PRE-DIFF fails only on findings new against --base; base findings are cached. It runs beside elab with in-bind PRE off; ADVISORY runs off the gating path.
  r8-prepass, then R8 refresh on the fork. Drift is reported as FIXED ("R8 drift fixed in N table(s)"), not as an error. One R8 bind loop runs if the strict bind still sees R8_STALE.
  Scoped strict bind (BIND-SPEED's scoped top + chunked emit), then lane latency.
  Writes <out>/ROW-READY.json (schema row-ready.v1) with plan sha, keys, table shas and per-step seconds, and copies it into --ledger.
  NORMALIZE alone: tools/die_plan/row_normalize.py plan|tables. Rows now carry intent only: no hand tapname_fix, retap, reprice or r8_refresh scripts.
  ROLLING COMPOSE: tools/die_plan/row_compose.py roll --die <die> --ledger <dir> --pub <dir> --asbuilt <rel> [--watch 600]. It applies every READY ledger row in a deterministic order on the current plan and gates the batch. A failing batch is bisected to the bad row. It publishes PUB/current.json + published/rNNN.json.

- 2026-11-25 07:09 PST [STAGE-PLATEAU -> FP-CONVERGE-KV, KV-PC-BANK; cc COORD] VIS verdict kv3_pc__cl254f2e73 PLACE-GP (epyc12, vis_review/place-gp-1125-1500): VERDICT-SMELL-MAJOR. 9 problems, all listed. Facts: die 1149x1521um, 8 hard cores (4 PCC 293x268um, 4 PCF 91x268um) + 4 SRAM, fill 0.263, std-cell util 2.0% (GPL-0019), GP timing-driven worst slack -583ps on an 833ps clock, 7643 pins. No flight_lines/rudy/macro_pg_overlay in kit/review (dir absent); paths.png has 0 paths drawn. Causes below are read from the renders, not traced in the netlist.
  1 UTILISATION. See: density map is ~0 over >90% of core; std cells are 2.0% of 1.72 mm2. Cause: outline is sized by the 2x4 core array pitch, not by logic. Fix: shrink the outline to the core array plus one 180um spine (drop the 245um top and bottom bands), or hand the freed bands to the parent as feedthrough area.
  2 DEAD BANDS. See: top band (245um above the cores) and bottom band (245um below) hold no cells except PG taps and 3 long horizontal buffer rows at the top. Cause: cores are centred vertically with equal margins and no logic owns the margins. Fix: move both core rows outward to the N/S edges (or cut the bands) so the only open area is the middle band where the logic is.
  3 CENTRE-SPINE HOT SPOT. See: the only dense cells (0.5+) are 20-40um strips glued to the inner E/W faces of all 4 PCC cores and at their inner corners, in a 183um spine; spine centre is empty. Cause: PCC signal pins all sit on the inner face, so every glue cell wants the same face strip. Fix: spread PCC pins along the full inner face at uniform pitch and put a pin-register column per core in the spine (region-constrained), not free placement.
  4 LONG PATHS / TIMING. See: GP worst slack -583ps with cells strung in diagonal chains from the W pin band toward the spine and 3 die-wide buffer rows across the top (~1000um). Cause: ports on W/E/N edges are 350-550um from the logic they talk to at the spine, with no pipeline station between. Fix: add one registered station row at each PCF outer face / top band (budgeted hop <=405um) or move those ports to the edge segment facing the spine.
  5 PIN CLUSTERING. See: W-edge pins occupy only y~530-1010um (about 31% of the face), E-edge pins two bands in the lower-middle, N-edge pins three short clusters plus a dense NE-corner block; S edge nearly empty. Cause: pin bands are inherited from parent seam slots without spreading to the free face length. Fix: re-pitch each bus over its whole face segment (or 2 layers) so pin density per um drops and landing flops do not stack.
  6 NW CORNER BLOB. See: an isolated ~85x60um block at density 0.5+ in the NW corner, >180um from any core, feeding a die-wide buffer row to the NE pin comb. Cause: a logic cluster is anchored to corner ports on N/W instead of to its consumer. Fix: move that port group next to the NE cluster it talks to (or place the block mid-top and register both ends).
  7 PCF-PCC CHANNELS. See: four 35um channels between each PCF and its PCC are empty of cells while halos take ~8um each side. Cause: channel is too narrow to be useful for logic and too wide to be an abutment. Fix: abut PCF to PCC (shared halo, pins through the abutted face) or widen to >=60um and assign the PCF-PCC pin registers there.
  8 PCF OUTBOARD, UNUSED FACES. See: PCF cores have no cells on their outer, top or bottom faces except a small cluster under the upper-right PCF; the 60um W/E margins outside them are empty. Cause: PCF sits between the W/E port band and the spine and blocks the direct route with no pins facing the ports. Fix: push PCF to the die edge (margin 0) so ports land on core-free edge segments in the middle band.
  9 SRAM PLACEMENT ASYMMETRY. See: 4 SRAMs sit in the middle band; cells gather beside the right pair and along x~620-700um, none by the left pair; halos are uneven. Cause: SRAMs are placed mirror-symmetric but their consumer logic is one-sided. Fix: stack the 4 SRAMs in one column on the spine axis next to that logic, pins facing it.
  Also: review inputs missing - add flight_lines/rudy/macro_pg_overlay to the PLACE-GP render so pin-face and congestion claims can be checked.

  6. Dense clump of cells at the block centre (x ~86um, y ~490um) on the dashed mid-height pin/tap row, with a thin vertical tail above it. Cause: reset/clock tap fan-out drivers all pulled to the single centre tap. Fix: drive the three station ranks from per-rank taps placed on each rank's diagonal instead of one centre tap.
